Prevention: Practice crop rotation with cotton for 2 to 3 years before going back to sunflower
Sow only recommended varieties if available (hysun 33 t40318 ; S-278; HI- Sun 39; Golden-01; SF-187; SF-177; CRN-1435; SH-3322;FH-331, DK40:40)
Irrigate more during the hot and dry season of the year to avoid water stress
Collect and destroy residues of past crops before planting for next season
Monitoring: The symptoms are generally not seen until after flowering stage and show as silver gray spots on the stalk near the soil line.
Losses are often observed during the hot and dry season.
Affected plants become smaller and dry up if the problem is severe.
Affected plants have smaller than normal leaves, reduced vigor and improper seed formation.
Monitor the crop twice a week during the hot and dry season.
Insects and hail damage can promote the spread of the disease.
In severe attacks, plants die before seed set.
Direct Control: Remove infected plants and seeds from field after harvesting as this disease can hibernate in seeds and diseased plant debris.
Uproot infected plants carefully and burn them away from the field.
Conserve soil moisture by reducing plant populations, practicing minimum tillage and controlling weeds.
Restrictions: Wear protective clothing when spraying dangerous chemicals (masks, boots, gloves…)
Do not eat or smoke when spraying chemicals.
Spray thiophanate- methyl @ 2g/Litre water when symptoms appear
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use).
Spraying on appearance of the symptoms may prevent further spread of the disease .
Seed treatment with thiophanate-methyl or carbendazem @ 2g/Kg seed
